title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.17110v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for latent actions. translated_title: SALA：语义对齐的潜在动作实现具身基础模型的双轴扩展
translated_abstract: 具身基础模型依赖于多样化的机器人交互数据，而这些数据的收集成本高昂。以自我为中心的人类视频提供了一种互补的经验来源，而潜在动作模型（LAM）则是利用这些视频进行策略监督的一种流行方法。与世界-动作模型（WAM）相比，LAM通过在策略学习和执行过程中避免显式的像素预测，能够提供更高的训练效率和更低的推理成本。然而，现有的LAM大多仅通过视频重建来学习潜在动作，这可能导致其表示按照视觉外观而非底层动作进行聚类，从而难以将人类动作与对应的机器人动作对齐。为了弥合这一差距，我们提出了SALA，它强调为潜在动作建立语义对应关系。在无需配对数据的情况下，我们利用未配对的人类和……的语言描述（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: SALA通过为潜在动作建立语义对应关系而非依赖视频重建，在无需配对数据的情况下实现了人类动作与机器人动作的有效对齐，从而支持具身基础模型的双轴扩展。
en_tdlr: SALA establishes semantic correspondence for latent actions without requiring paired data, enabling effective alignment between human and robot actions and supporting dual-axis scaling of embodied foundation models.
